headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared project files and plugin-driven orchestration; no critical compliance issue evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and Semantic Kernel can consume application-defined files and MCP/OpenAPI tool outputs. That creates a default pathway where attacker-controlled content from agent_a can be read by agent_b as instructions. The pair lacks provenance tracking or isolation by default, so the interaction is plausible without unusual setup.
conditions: IF agent_b reads agent_a-written files as prompts or tool instructions
IF both agents operate in the same project directory without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Prefix all inter-agent files with a machine-readable provenance header
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from shared files
Review any file passed from agent_a before agent_b consumes it
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a can read and write the project directory and has broad network egress; agent_b can read files and call external model providers or MCP servers. Even though the profiles only name generated source code and application context, shared workspace plus outbound API calls creates a default leakage path for file contents into third-party inference backends.
conditions: IF sensitive material is placed in the shared project directory
IF agent_b forwards file contents to a model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory
Use separate workspaces per agent
Turn off file-upload or retrieval plugins for agent_b
Redact sensitive files before either agent reads them
requires-engineering: enforce per-file access controls and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write access, and agent_a shares state via the project directory while agent_b shares state via a memory store. That overlapping mutable surface can cause write races or stale overwrites even without git locking, especially when agent_b also uses plugins and external tools. The conflict is real in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project files
IF the orchestrator does not serialize writes or lock shared resources
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths to each agent
Serialize write operations through one coordinator
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Avoid concurrent edits to the same document
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a writes files and can execute generated code, while agent_b is a plugin-driven orchestrator that can act on application context and external tool outputs. If agent_b treats agent_a's generated artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream actions or code execution. The default pair lacks a built-in verification step, so the blast radius is substantial.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as trusted input without validation
IF generated code or facts from agent_a are executed or forwarded by agent_b
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Add a verification step between agents
Limit agent_b to summarizing rather than acting on agent_a output
Run agent_a in a non-executable sandbox
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch generated source code and application context, so no specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced. However, agent_a handles OPENAI_API_KEY and agent_b handles plugin credentials, so a compliance issue could arise if those secrets are placed into shared files or logs. The other agent is not cited because no regulated-data flow is documented.
conditions: IF secrets are stored in shared project files or logs
IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workspace
mitigations: Keep API keys in environment variables only
Exclude secrets from shared files and logs
Use separate retention policies for each workspace
Review plugin logging settings
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning and retention enforcement
